entities.summary:
John of Beverley was an English bishop active in the kingdom of Northumbria. He was the bishop of Hexham and then the bishop of York, which was the most important religious designation in the area. He went on to found the town of Beverley by building the first structure there, a monastery. John was associated with miracles during and after his lifetime and was canonised a saint by the Catholic Church in 1037.

As this is prior to the Great East–West Schism of 1054, he is also recognised as a saint by the Eastern Orthodox Church. John of Beverley was a religious figures from Harpham (700 CE, Harpham–721-05-11). Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: John of Beverley's founding of the monastery in Beverley had a lasting impact on the region, as it became a major pilgrimage site and helped establish the town as an important center of Christianity. His canonization as a saint by both the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Churches underscores his significance across multiple Christian traditions.
